findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in init workers
findings.body: The errgroup closures run concurrently. They all assign to the outer `err` with `_, _, err = s.build(...)`, and they all do `totalBatchesIndexed++` without synchronization. This is a data race, and it is now on the startup path. The reported `namespaced_indexed` count can also be wrong. Use a local error variable and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Blocking Init in constructor with a cancelable background ctx; stale/hanging failure modes
findings.body: NewResourceServer now runs the full search index build synchronously, so construction blocks until every namespace is indexed. If anything fails, the whole server fails to construct. Previously this failure only surfaced on the first request. The lifecycle `Init` also runs here with the server's own context. Startup time and failure semantics change significantly, and the PR's own question about lazy-init dependents remains unanswered. The `Init` call to `lifecycle.Init` can also run before the SQL backend has been set up by other callers.

findings.title: Concurrent builds of same key can race and leak/overwrite index
findings.body: Removing the lock around the whole of BuildIndex means two concurrent builds for the same key can both run. For file-backed indexes, `bleve.New(dir)` fails for the second caller because the directory already exists. For memory indexes, the second build silently overwrites the first in the cache and leaks it. `getOrCreateIndex` is a check-then-build with no dedup. Previously the lock serialized this.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without lock
findings.body: `TotalDocs` reads `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. Builds can now write to the map concurrently, and `init` calls `TotalDocs` in a new log line. A concurrent map read and write can cause a fatal runtime error.

findings.title: Test skipped for postgres instead of fixed
findings.body: The integration test is now skipped for postgres to work around a failure that is probably caused by the eager init change. This reduces coverage rather than addressing the cause.
